messages.subject: Re: Is WordCount.R executing against my Cluster Hadoop or JobRunner Local? Configuration for Cluster?
parts:
rmr2 picks whatever configuration hadoop has. So if you set the env variable HADOOP_CMD to /usr/loca/bin/hadoop and when you use that command, it runs in standalone mode, rmr2 will run in standalone mode. Same for distributed and pseudodistributed modes. So I would first make sure that HADOOP_CMD is pointing where you expect and then look up the documentation for CDH4 searching  for "configure distributed mode". I am sure also there are Cloudera user forums and Hadoop user forums where you will find better answers than here. But if you configure Hadoop right and rmr is using the Hadoop copy that you think it is using (this is a problem if you have multiple hadoop installed, like I do) rmr2 doesn't have any additional configuration. Of course there is the backend choice, but rmr starts on the hadoop backend by default and that doesn't sound like your problem. Just to be super cautions, you could check rmr.options("backend") . It should return "hadoop". I hope this helps


Antonio

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#776] Re: Is WordCount.R executing against my Cluster Hadoop or JobRunner Local? Configuration for Cluster?
parts:
On Thu, May 30, 2013 at 8:09 AM, Miguel Romero <miguel.rom...@gmail.com> wrote:
there is no package called 'rmr2'

You need to install rmr2 and all its dependencies on each node of the cluster. If you've done that already, you may have a problem like in that thread that R doesn't find them, and that's an issue with users and directories. I always recommend installing packages for every user in the most standard locations. People who diligently follow instructions for an unprivileged install need to realize that they may have user account johnstat, but the jobs and hence map process hence R interpreter is going to run as user hadoop or mapred, a dedicated user created by the hadoop install process. That requires a modified .libPaths in R. There is no special feature to set that in rmr2 but it should be possible using standard R configuration files. That's as much as I know about it. Of course I would encourage anybody to do a standard install for every user, that way one install serves many people, everyone is happier in the long run.


Antonio
